/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 27 July 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2696 (-47)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4200 (-85)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1999 (-25)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1670 (-24)
Baltic Handysize Index: 903 (-2)
CAPESIZE
A rather lacklustre start to the week saw the market lose a little momentum, with Monday’s trading characterised by limited activity and a cautious “wait-and-watch” approach from both owners and charterers. The BCI 182 5TC declined by $770, closing at $38,090, with the C5 index slipping $0.230 to $12.625, while C3 dipped $0.320 to $34.360. In the Pacific, sentiment was marginally softer amid limited activity. Only one major miner was active on C5, although operators continued to provide a reasonable flow of cargoes. Offers began the day around $13.00 to the low-to-mid $13s, but sentiment weakened after a miner entered the market bidding $12.00. As the session progressed, owners gradually softened their ideas, with offers reportedly falling below $13.00 and discussion of $12.65 being offered. No fixtures had been reported at the time of writing. The Atlantic also started the week on a quieter note. South Atlantic and West Africa saw a modest correction with limited fresh business, while the North Atlantic experienced very little activity and sentiment softened slightly. On C3, offers were heard around $34.50 on index dates, although there were no corresponding bids, highlighting the cautious mood. As is often the case on a Monday, many market participants appeared content to assess conditions before committing.
PANAMAX
A sluggish start to the week in the Atlantic, with brokers commenting that activity has been relatively minimal. Market sources have stated that some fresh cargo has entered the market today for trans-Atlantic business, and while the prompt tonnage count remains tight off the North Continent, sentiment continues to lean to the negative side. Owners are said to continue favouring business that keeps them within the Atlantic basin and, for now, most participants appear to be evaluating the market's direction before entering into firm negotiations. Reported fronthaul fixtures increasingly appear to be fixing on a split-rate basis for redelivery. The Saita I (81,922 2014) fixed basis delivery Haldia 21 July for a fronthaul grains trip via East Coast South America at $19,500 basis redelivery Southeast Asia and $19,750 basis redelivery North China to Bunge. Some market sources suggest that the Pacific may be nearing a rate floor, with reported fixtures further strengthening this view. Activity is also said to have picked up compared to the previous week, although the tonnage count remains significant, and a substantial increase in fresh cargo will be required to shift sentiment and support a more positive outlook. The P5TC fell by $223 today to $17,990.
SUPRAMAX
The Index was aggressively marked for a Monday, with the 11TC average down $302 to $21,106. In keeping with the last 2 weeks the North American routes were the hardest hit, especially with news of an Ultramax fixing on Friday for a trip UK-Continent with woodpellets at $25,000. The Continent continued with limited activity, although many felt levels were only slightly softer, and the East Mediterranean which had remained firm lately was now said to be more balanced, but rates are currently maintained. In the South the lengthening tonnage list means Charterers are able to be more fussy and sources said eco Ultramax’s were being preferred due to current bunker increases, whilst the smaller/older types are beginning to struggle slightly. The Indian Ocean has been holding up with decent mineral demand from South Africa, but further East rates have softened with NoPac and Australia both slowing and not giving the same support now to the backhaul market. For now Indonesian levels look similar with the Apollo.GR (60,437 2016) Singapore 1-3 August said to be on subjects for a trip via Indonesia up to China at $19,500, but the Charterer remained private.
HANDYSIZE
The market started the week with a mixed performance, with positional sentiment prevailing across the regions. The BHSI edged down by 2 points to 903, while the 7TC average slipped by $35 to settle at $16,255. Across the Continent and Mediterranean last week’s trend persisted, with limited new enquiry resulting in subdued activity. The US Gulf and South Atlantic opened on a softer note, with rates continuing to ease on the back of a growing tonnage count. Across Asia the market remained positive, supported by a healthy balance between tonnage availability and cargo demand in key loading regions.

Atlantic
The Rostrum Australia (40,017 2023) was fixed for a trip delivery Recalada for fronthaul business at $22,500. The Fedra GR (37,301 2020) was placed on subjects for a trip from Norfolk to the Continent at $19,000 by Bunge, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
The Novena WW (32,503 2012), open Shimizu on 24 July was fixed for a trip to West Coast India at $25,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
Chinese Crude Steel Production

In the period 11-20 July, daily crude steel production at Chinese Iron and Steel Association (CISA) member mills eased 0.4% from the preceding ten days to 2.0 Mt, according to the industry association. Meanwhile, output stood 5.9% lower than the same period last year. Major steel mills’ inventory climbed 8.1% from early-July to 18.1 Mt in mid-July, the highest since mid-May. In the week to 24 July, Chinese iron ore stockpiles declined for the fourth consecutive week, down 0.1 Mt to 162.7 Mt, according to data from 42 portside locations monitored by Umetal.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The front end of the Cape FFA curve lost significant value today in response to a falling physical market, with the weakest contract being the Aug by far, with 31500 sold, followed by the Sep down to 34750. The Oct and Q4 were very well supported in contrast, with the Oct trading up to 36000 and closing marginally positive. The Q4 was similar, with a high of 35250 trading and also the Q1 with 24650 paid. The Cals were thin today with talk of 29000 being paid cape cal27.
